Debian packages the same Windows-produced emitter WVB and executes that native compiler on real Debian. This is not independent compiler-source reconstruction.

The owned helper is validated before dead-function elimination but not invoked at runtime. These three cases do not establish general owned Vector payload execution, release behavior, exclusive borrow, Take, or Map.

The old construction emitter passes the first two selector cases but rejects copy-borrow-return as Invalid_analysis/Invalid_wir. This expected differential failure demonstrates the new case detects the corrected behavior; it is not a passing baseline run.

The full Generic-WIR self-test construction remains incomplete: ordinary analysis exhausted instructions and a whitespace-compacted Profile 8 diagnostic reached the existing five-minute timeout before assertions ran. No limits were increased. The emitter's full directory validator was instead exercised through Source-Emission-Core and Source-Analysis-Validation-Core; this does not claim all Generic-WIR test assertions passed.
Recorded fixture WVB hashes equal the earlier native-executed record and text products; no new native execution or complete WVB 1.39 admission is claimed by this record.
